message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"14f76aea816b30c32eacfcc31c3ecce0e6088fda0ba8b828996ef3e1d04d40ff","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:62","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","units":[{"unit_id":"sec08-u01","module_id":"sec08-m01","objective_ids":["sec08-u01"],"title":{"text":"Sign basics, stops and yields","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every driver must recognize signs instantly and obey regulatory signs without hesitating.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F05"]},{"text":"Four-way stops and yield signs decide who goes first, so knowing the rules prevents collisions.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F09"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same moment, one on the left and one on the right.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When vehicles reach a four-way stop together, the one farthest to the right goes first.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F06"]},"result":{"text":"The car on the right goes first, and the other driver still waits a few seconds to be sure no one else starts in.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that once it is your turn at a four-way stop you can go without looking.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08"]},"correction":{"text":"Even on your turn, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts in, because many drivers ignore the rule.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"First to stop goes first; ties go right.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"At a four-way stop, which vehicle may go first when the arrivals are at different times?","fact_ids":["sec08-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"The first vehicle to come to a complete stop.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06"]},"rationale":{"text":"Vehicles leave a four-way stop in the order they arrived.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Why signs matter","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Know signs instantly.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03"]},{"text":"Three types of signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every driver must know signs, signals and road markings well enough to recognize them instantly and to obey regulatory signs without hesitating. Signs now use more symbols and pictures, because those can be recognized faster at higher speeds and from farther away. A sign's shape and color are both coded to the kind of message it carries, so you should learn shapes and colors as well as the individual signs. In this lesson you will meet the three sign types, the rules for four-way stops and yield signs, and several regulatory signs about entering and turning.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three types of signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F04","sec08-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Regulatory, warning, guide.","fact_ids":["sec08-F04","sec08-F05"]},{"text":"Regulatory signs must be obeyed.","fact_ids":["sec08-F04","sec08-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Traffic signs fall into three types by function: regulatory signs, warning signs, and information or guide signs. Regulatory signs control how traffic moves. They are black and white unless they are shown in their actual color, and they must be obeyed. Warning signs, which you will meet in later lessons, alert you to hazards ahead. Guide signs give information and directions. Knowing which type a sign belongs to tells you right away whether it is giving you a rule you must follow, a hazard to prepare for, or information to help you find your way.","fact_ids":["sec08-F04","sec08-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The four-way stop","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"First to stop goes first.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]},{"text":"Ties go to the right.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"At a four-way stop, vehicles leave in the order they arrived, so the first one to come to a complete stop is the first one allowed to go. When two or more vehicles reach the four-way stop at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first. And even when it is your turn, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule. These three rules together handle almost every four-way stop you will meet, and they are a favorite topic for test questions. Regulatory signs must be obeyed.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Yield and wrong way","fact_ids":["sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"YIELD: slow and give way.","fact_ids":["sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11"]},{"text":"White on red: wrong direction.","fact_ids":["sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"A YIELD sign tells you to slow down so you can give the right of way to pedestrians crossing and to vehicles on the intersecting road. A white-on-red regulatory sign warns that you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction. Another regulatory sign marks a one-way roadway whose traffic is coming toward you, and you may not enter it at that point. These signs protect you from head-on crashes, so if you ever see a wrong-way warning, you should stop and change direction safely rather than continue onto the road. Regulatory signs must be obeyed.","fact_ids":["sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Your turn still means look","fact_ids":["sec08-F08","sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Arrival order decides turns.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08","sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]},{"text":"Wait a few seconds anyway.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08","sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Knowing the four-way stop order is not the same as being safe. Vehicles leave in the order they arrived, and when they arrive together the one farthest to the right goes first. But even when it is your turn, you should wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule. So a question that asks what to do when it is your turn is looking for that extra check: confirm that no one else is pulling out before you go, rather than assuming everyone knows the order.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08","sec08-F06","sec08-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the four-way order","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Who goes first at different arrivals?","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: at a four-way stop, which vehicle may go first when the arrivals are at different times? Decide on your answer first. The answer is the first vehicle to come to a complete stop, because vehicles leave in the order they arrived. If vehicles arrive at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first. And whoever is next should still check that no one else starts into the intersection. Remember these three rules together: arrival order, ties to the right, and a short wait to check. Regulatory signs must be obeyed.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06","sec08-F07","sec08-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Sign basics recap","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-F05","sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F12","sec08-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Railroad and no-left-turn signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-F05","sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F12","sec08-F13"]},{"text":"Obey regulatory signs every time.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-F05","sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F12","sec08-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, know signs well enough to recognize them instantly and obey regulatory signs without hesitating. Symbols are faster to read, and shape and color code the message. The three types are regulatory, warning and guide signs, and regulatory signs are black and white unless shown in actual color. At a four-way stop the first to stop goes first and ties go right, but you still check that no one else is starting in. A YIELD sign means slow and give way. The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear, and a no-left-turn sign means you may not turn left there.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-F05","sec08-F09","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F12","sec08-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec08-u02","module_id":"sec08-m02","objective_ids":["sec08-u02"],"title":{"text":"Parking and speed signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Parking and speed signs set rules you must follow even when the road looks clear.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F16","sec08-F19"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Chris wants to wait in the car beside a no-parking sign while a friend runs into a store.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area even if you remain inside the car.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14"]},"result":{"text":"Chris must find a legal space instead, because staying in the car does not make it legal.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a handicapped space is fine as long as the sticker is somewhere in the car.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15"]},"correction":{"text":"The vehicle must be driven or directed by a handicapped person and must visibly show the handicapped sticker.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"No parking means no parking, even sitting inside.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver wants to stop to check a map beside an EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign. Is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec08-F16"]},"answer":{"text":"No, stopping there is allowed only for real emergencies.","fact_ids":["sec08-F16"]},"rationale":{"text":"The sign allows stopping only for real emergencies, not for errands or calls.","fact_ids":["sec08-F16"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Rules for stopping and speed","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Parking signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19"]},{"text":"Speed signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers regulatory signs about where you may stop or park and how fast you may go. You will learn what a no-parking sign really means, the conditions for using a space reserved for the physically handicapped, and the emergency-stopping-only sign. Then you will see what a posted speed limit means, how maximum and minimum speed signs work, and when a school-zone speed limit applies. Each of these is a regulatory sign, which means you must obey it whether or not the road looks clear and whether or not anyone is watching. These regulatory signs must be obeyed as written.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Parking signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"No parking, even sitting in the car.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16"]},{"text":"Handicapped spaces need two conditions.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area, even if you remain inside the car. You may not park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped, on public or private property, unless a handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle and the vehicle visibly shows the handicapped sticker. Both conditions are required. An EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign allows stopping only for real emergencies. Each of these signs leaves no room for exceptions like a quick errand, so treat them as firm rules every time you see them. These regulatory signs must be obeyed as written.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Speed limit signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"Posted limit: normal conditions.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},{"text":"Minimums mostly on freeways.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"A posted speed limit is the speed allowed under normal conditions. A sign reading SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed in that area. Some signs post both a maximum and a minimum speed for a stretch of highway, and minimum limits usually appear on freeways and other controlled-access highways. A school-zone speed limit applies during the hours the sign shows, and it may also be displayed on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights. So check the sign for hours, flashing lights or a minimum as well as the main number.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two conditions, not one","fact_ids":["sec08-F15","sec08-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"A driver or director with a disability.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15","sec08-F14"]},{"text":"A visible handicapped sticker.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15","sec08-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap with handicapped parking. Some drivers think a sticker anywhere in the car is enough, or that dropping off a passenger with a disability makes any car eligible. The manual sets two conditions that must both be met: a physically handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle, and the vehicle visibly shows the handicapped sticker. The rule applies on public and private property. And remember the no-parking rule: you may not park under a no-parking sign even if you stay in the car. Neither sign has an exception for a short wait.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15","sec08-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check emergency stopping","fact_ids":["sec08-F16","sec08-F14","sec08-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"When may you stop there?","fact_ids":["sec08-F16","sec08-F14","sec08-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: when may you stop where an EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign is posted? Decide first, then compare. The answer is only for real emergencies. The sign does not allow stopping to check a map, make a phone call or rest when traffic is light. Compare it with a no-parking sign, which forbids parking even if you stay in the car, and with handicapped spaces, which require both a qualifying driver or director and a visible sticker. Each of these regulatory signs must be obeyed exactly as written. These regulatory signs must be obeyed as written.","fact_ids":["sec08-F16","sec08-F14","sec08-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Parking and speed recap","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"No parking, even inside.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},{"text":"Speed signs: max, min, school hours.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, you may not park under a no-parking sign even if you stay in the car. A handicapped space requires a handicapped driver or director and a visible sticker, on public or private property. EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY allows stops only for real emergencies. A posted limit is the speed for normal conditions, so SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed. Some highways post a maximum and a minimum, with minimums usually on freeways and controlled-access highways, and school-zone limits apply during the posted hours, sometimes shown with flashing amber lights.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec08-u03","module_id":"sec08-m03","objective_ids":["sec08-u03"],"title":{"text":"Turn, lane and passing signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F22"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Turn and lane signs tell you which movements are allowed at an intersection before you reach it.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F25"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Pat waits at a red light where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted and wants to turn right.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Where NO TURN ON RED is posted at a signal, you may not turn right or left on a red light.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23"]},"result":{"text":"Pat waits for the green light before turning.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking double right turns are allowed at any intersection with two right lanes.","fact_ids":["sec08-F26"]},"correction":{"text":"Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; elsewhere the normal right-turn rules apply.","fact_ids":["sec08-F26"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"No turns means neither way; no turn on red means wait for green.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-F23"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"At an intersection with a NO TURNS sign, which ways may you turn?","fact_ids":["sec08-F18"]},"answer":{"text":"Neither right nor left; you may not turn there.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18"]},"rationale":{"text":"A NO TURNS sign bans both turns, unlike a no-left-turn sign, which bans only left turns.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-F13"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Signs that control turns","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F27"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lane-use and turn signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F27"]},{"text":"Passing and direction signs.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F27"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers regulatory signs that decide which way you may go. You will see signs that require a lane to turn, signs that forbid turns, the NO TURN ON RED sign, the rule for double right turns, the sign that tells you not to drive to its left, the one-way arrow sign, and the regulatory sign that marks where a no-passing zone begins. Reading these signs early lets you get into the right lane well before the intersection, so you are not forced into a last-moment lane change or an illegal turn. Read lane-use signs early so you are in the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F27"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Lane and turn signs","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F25","sec08-F26"]},"lines":[{"text":"Left lane must turn left.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F25","sec08-F26"]},{"text":"No turns: neither right nor left.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F25","sec08-F26"]}],"narration":{"text":"A LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign means traffic in the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead. A NO TURNS sign means you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection. A lane-use sign can require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight. Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; at unsigned intersections the normal right-turn rules apply. So look at the lane-use signs as you approach and choose your lane by where you need to go. Read lane-use signs early so you are in the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F25","sec08-F26"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Red lights, direction and passing","fact_ids":["sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F27","sec08-F22"]},"lines":[{"text":"No turn on red where posted.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F27","sec08-F22"]},{"text":"Follow the one-way arrow.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F27","sec08-F22"]}],"narration":{"text":"Where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted at a signal-controlled intersection, you may not turn right or left on a red light. One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to the left of it, so you keep to its right. A one-way arrow sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points. And one regulatory sign marks where a no-passing zone begins. Each of these limits a movement: turning on red, passing a sign on the wrong side, driving against the arrow, or passing in the zone that begins at the sign. Read lane-use signs early so you are in the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F27","sec08-F22"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Double right turns","fact_ids":["sec08-F26","sec08-F25"]},"lines":[{"text":"Only where signed.","fact_ids":["sec08-F26","sec08-F25"]},{"text":"Otherwise normal right-turn rules.","fact_ids":["sec08-F26","sec08-F25"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. When a road has two right lanes, some drivers assume both may always turn right. The manual says double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them. At intersections without that signing, the normal right-turn rules apply. A lane-use sign may require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight, and that is the kind of sign that permits two lanes to turn. Without such a sign, do not turn right from the second lane, even if the intersection looks wide. Read lane-use signs early so you are in the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F26","sec08-F25"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the no turns sign","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"What does NO TURNS mean?","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: what does a NO TURNS sign mean? Decide on your answer first. The answer is that you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection. Compare it with a no-left-turn sign, which bans only left turns, and with a NO TURN ON RED sign, which bans right and left turns only while the light is red. Each of these signs bans a different set of movements, so read the sign carefully. If a question shows a NO TURNS sign, the only choice left is to go straight through the intersection. Read lane-use signs early so you are in the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-F23","sec08-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Turn and lane recap","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F22","sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F25","sec08-F26","sec08-F27"]},"lines":[{"text":"Read lane signs early.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F22","sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F25","sec08-F26","sec08-F27"]},{"text":"Know which turns each sign bans.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F22","sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F25","sec08-F26","sec08-F27"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT means the left lane turns left at the intersection ahead, and NO TURNS means no right and no left. A lane-use sign can make the right lane turn right while the next lane may turn or go straight, and double right turns are allowed only where signed. NO TURN ON RED bans right and left turns on red at a signal.
